local_coconet_health.description: Inspect this project’s local processing, replica and search coverage when an operation is blocked or the user asks about sync. Background issues do not imply a selected source is unavailable; use its Read/Pull result. Detailed logs are available through coconet projection status --json and coconet diagnostics list.

local_read_project_work_graph.description: Read the verified local project DAG and committed Session open items without downloading conversations. Inspect processing coverage and node relations status: pending relations are not confirmed independent roots. Select a node and its exact source for pull_session before relying on implementation or verification claims. Follow next_cursor to inspect additional pages; restart when the selected results change between pages.

local_search_work.description: Search accepted node text, Library notes and locally indexed user/assistant conversation text in the project connected to this folder (coconet connect). query requires 1–4000 nonblank characters and at most 64 whitespace-separated literal terms; matches any term. limit is 1–100, default 10; use next_cursor for more results. No model call or network download is needed. Inspect index coverage and revision: missing or unindexed copies make results partial. content_matches contain an exact source, turn_id, ordinal and snippet; work_node_ids may be empty while processing is pending. Repeated cumulative prefixes are deduplicated. Read the selected compact source before relying on detailed claims. Restart without a cursor if the query or selected results change.

local_pull_session.description: Read an exact retained source into compact_path, using verified local copies first. Copy source (session_id, version) from graph or search results, and include work_node_id when selecting a node. A synchronized source can be read with include_artifact or continued before a DAG node exists. A changed node source requires a refreshed selection. Missing temporary cloud content enters peer repair; waiting is not successful download. Runtime replicates retained project Sessions in the background.

local_list_library_entries.description: Browse explicitly collected fixed nodes, notes and sources in the local project Library without downloading conversations. Follow next_cursor to inspect additional pages; restart when the selected Library results change. Collection does not imply completion.

local_add_session_to_library.description: Only on explicit user request, collect any accessible Work Node and its exact source from the local graph. Supply request_id, work_node_id, source and an optional note. This saves the selected source and display independently; the author node can continue updating. Collection does not mark work complete. Reuse the same request_id and all original arguments after timeout. A changed source requires refreshing the graph and a new request_id. This tool does not capture an unprocessed live Session.

local_fork_session.description: Only on explicit user request, create a separate Session in the current Agent (Codex, Claude or Cursor) from an exact synchronized source. Same-Agent Fork preserves native history; cross-Agent Fork transfers effective user/assistant text only, excluding tools, reasoning and media. Supply a stable request_id and source; include work_node_id when selecting a node. Reuse all original arguments after timeout; retries preserve the child identity. This uses verified local history, downloads missing content as needed, preserves workspace files and source history, and returns native_session_id plus a resume command. Success means the local Session is ready; project synchronization continues in the background. Inherited dialogue is saved as baseline, not new work; subsequent conversation is processed after that baseline synchronizes. Return the resume command; the user chooses when to switch conversations.

local_remove_session_from_library.description: Only on explicit user request, remove a selected entry from Session Library using a stable request_id, work_node_id and exact saved source from the Library listing (or node.library.source on the current graph). Reuse all original arguments after timeout. This changes the bookmark only, without changing the author node or native history. Unreferenced cached content may later be reclaimed.
